data.summary: This 12‑week plan tackles the student’s weak units first, interleaving review and practice, and reserves the final two weeks for mixed review and timed practice. Each week is capped at 6 hours and includes concrete tasks that can be completed in a single sitting.
data.final_week_advice: Use the last two weeks for full‑length practice exams, timed problem sets, and targeted review of any remaining weak spots. Focus on pacing, error analysis, and reinforcing conceptual links across units.

tasks: Do 10 multiple‑choice questions on molar mass and atomic structure, then check answers against the scoring guide
Sketch electron configurations for 5 elements and label valence electrons
Solve 8 problems on mass spectroscopy data interpretation
Create a table comparing elemental composition of 3 pure substances
Draw Lewis structures for 6 molecules, noting formal charges
Classify 4 compounds as ionic, covalent, or metallic
Match 5 substances to their dominant intermolecular forces
Explain why ice floats using solid structure concepts
Calculate pressure changes using the ideal gas law in 4 scenarios
Solve 6 stoichiometry problems involving gas reactions
Plot concentration vs. time data for 3 reactions
Determine rate laws for 4 reactions from given data
Draw energy diagrams for 3 endothermic and exothermic processes
Calculate heat changes using calorimetry equations
Compute Q and K for 3 reactions, predict direction
Set up and solve equilibrium expressions for 2 systems
Calculate pH for 4 strong acid/base solutions
Determine Ka and Kb for 3 weak acids/bases
Compute ΔG for 3 reactions, relate to spontaneity
Sketch cell diagrams for 2 galvanic cells and calculate E°
Take a 60‑minute timed practice quiz covering all units
Review incorrect answers and rewrite explanations
Complete a full-length 90‑minute practice exam under test conditions
Analyze performance, identify remaining weak areas, and plan brief review sessions
